revisionDesc.change: Created by Mitchell Harrop with Claude (AI-assisted), from the four sheets used to place the 1920s records.

div.p: The Mahlstedt plans are fire insurance plans. G. Mahlstedt and Son, civil engineers and surveyors, drew them for the Insurance Planning Association so that insurers could judge the fire risk of each building without visiting it. Every building is drawn to scale and coloured by what it is built of, with its number of storeys in a circle, the roof, the floors, fire walls, lifts and sprinklers, and often the name of the firm inside. Water mains are marked in the streets and fire plugs as small circles along the kerbs.

The City of Melbourne series covers the city and its inner suburbs in numbered sheets. The four sheets used here were drawn between 1923 and 1928, about thirty years after the Melbourne and Metropolitan Board of Works plans, and show Carlton as the factories and motor garages were moving in among the cottages: the Myer Emporium's despatch garage on Barry Street, Carlton & United Breweries on Swanston Street, the Tasmanian Timber Bending Works and Hopkins Bros. & Odlum on Leicester Street, Robert Bodington's millwright and engineering works on the corner of Queensberry and Leicester Streets, and motor showrooms all along Elizabeth Street.

Because they print the street number on almost every building, the plans can be matched to the directories and electoral rolls of the 1920s. Comparing them with the MMBW plans also shows where the street numbers changed between the 1890s and the 1920s: Madeline Street had become part of Swanston Street, with the numbers 516 higher on the west side; Leicester Street south of Queensberry Street and part of Bouverie Street near Alma Place had been renumbered; and Alma Place no longer reached Leicester Street. In October 2026 Mitchell Harrop and Claude (AI-assisted) read the house numbers off the four sheets and used them to place or check about 1,000 directory and roll listings from 1919 to 1945. How the points were worked out is in the project's data notes.
The sheets used in the project are as follows:

● Sheet 18A: Queensberry Street to Victoria Street, between Bouverie Street and Cardigan Street, including both sides of Swanston Street (Nos. 442–520 and 515–597), Ballarat Street, Storey Place, Cornell Place, Cardigan Terrace and the Carlton & United Breweries.

● Sheet 19A: Queensberry Street to Victoria Street, between Elizabeth Street and Bouverie Street, including Elizabeth Street Nos. 518–608, Berkley Street, Leicester Street, Lansdowne Place and Alma Place.

● Sheet 21A: Pelham Street to Queensberry Street, between Leicester Street and Swanston Street, including Bouverie Street, Lincoln Square South, Swanston Street Nos. 599–645, and Leicester, Barkly, Cumberland, Lincoln and Carlton Places.
● Sheet 22A: Pelham Street to Queensberry Street, between Elizabeth Street and Leicester Street, including Elizabeth Street Nos. 614–694, Berkley Street and Barry Street.
○ City of Melbourne plans, Section 2, State Library Victoria
